---
title: "AI-Assisted Federal Survey Harmonization"
subtitle: "Cross-Survey Integration Analysis of 47 Census Bureau Demographic Surveys"
date: today
abstract: |
  The Census Bureau fields 47 demographic survey instruments containing approximately 7,000 questions, each designed for a specific analytical purpose. No comprehensive map has existed showing where these surveys overlap, where their questions are compatible, and where the differences matter. This research uses AI-assisted methods --- multiple models from competing vendors independently rating question pairs with structured arbitration for disagreements --- to build that map at scale. Across two major survey pairs (CPS and FoodAPS, each scored against ACS), approximately 45% of questions have at least one viable harmonization path: roughly 16% are directly interchangeable through simple recoding, roughly 29% are linkable with documented statistical adjustments, and roughly 55% measure fundamentally different constructs. Harmonization rates are stable across survey pairs, suggesting a general property of the data rather than a survey-specific artifact. The complete analysis was conducted in weeks at a total API cost under \$100. The full pipeline, data, and code are public and reproducible.

  **DRAFT** --- These results are preliminary and have not been independently validated or peer reviewed. Full methodology, data, and code: [github.com/brockwebb/federal-survey-concept-mapper](https://github.com/brockwebb/federal-survey-concept-mapper). The views expressed are the author's own and do not necessarily represent the views of the U.S. Census Bureau or the U.S. Department of Commerce.
